ARCHITECT REVIEW OF THE PARK — IT IS CORRECT, AND HERE IS THE EXACT RULING STILL OWED. architect-a69740e0, 2026-08-28, measured at HEAD 0bf353ff. I considered promoting this row to PLANNING and decided against it on measurement. Recording that so the next reader inherits the answer instead of re-deriving it.

=== WHY I LOOKED ===
This row sits in BACKLOG, which no agent role can claim, and its filing says: "Promote it only when a governor or human has ruled on the design question in constraint (2)/(3)." The governor's CARRY ruling (comment-6a8d5bd8 on the parent) already exists and is cited in the description, so the question was whether that ruling discharges the gate. It does not — it settles one half and leaves the other genuinely open.

=== WHAT THE CARRY RULING DOES SETTLE ===
It defines COMPLETE as PER-LINEAGE completeness measured at supersede time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes, and it settles that CARRY STAYS UNEMITTABLE (an unchanged node is REQUALIFY; CARRY needs evaluateCarryForward's seven durable readers, none of which exist — that surface belongs to task-08efb6f0). Constraint (2)'s "derive the kind from durable state rather than a hardcoded literal" follows directly from it: the ruling names the predecessor/successor hash pair as the source, so un-hardcoding `kind: "ADD"` is ordinary engineering, not a design question.
Measured at HEAD, that constraint still holds: `supersession-preparation-history.ts:126-137` `lineageFactsFor` maps every lineage to a literal `kind: "ADD"` (:131), through an `as unknown as SupersessionNodeFacts` cast at :136.

=== WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, AND WHY THIS IS NOT ORDINARY ENGINEERING ===
Constraint (3) is a DELIBERATE FAIL-CLOSED AUTHORITY FENCE with its reasoning written into the code, not an incidental single-node limit. `journey-authority-bodies.ts` `graphContentOf` states it verbatim:
  "The journey's graph: ONE execution-bearing node, zero edges, keyed by the journey's own node, so two journeys naming different nodes seal different graphs rather than colliding on one content-addressed body row."
  "Fail CLOSED rather than silently dropping: the snapshot is single-node by design, so a caller passing two would seal a plan naming both against a graph that contains one of them."
  `if (nodeKey === undefined || extra.length > 0) throw new Error(...)`
So the throw exists to prevent a SEALED PLAN NAMING NODES ITS GRAPH DOES NOT CONTAIN, and to keep two journeys from colliding on one content-addressed body row. DoD-2 of this row asks for "journey-authority-bodies accepts the node ids a real multi-node graph produces" — that is a request to remove that fence. Removing it changes what a sealed journey graph MEANS and reopens both hazards the comment names. An agent may implement a multi-node producer; an agent may not decide that a fail-closed integrity fence should come down. That is the same shape as the (a)/(b) ruling the human took on the parent, and it is why this row's filing demanded a ruling in the first place.

=== THE QUESTION, PUT PRECISELY SO IT CAN BE ANSWERED IN ONE LINE ===
May the journey graph producer emit MULTI-NODE graphs — i.e. may `graphContentOf`'s single-node throw be replaced by a real multi-node snapshot — and if so, what replaces the two guarantees its comment currently provides: (i) that a sealed plan never names a node its graph lacks, and (ii) that two journeys naming different nodes cannot collide on one content-addressed body row?
Until that is answered, DoD-2 and DoD-3 are unreachable by construction, exactly as the parent measured. The parent task-7eddd612 is DONE at 8/8 with its delivered half graded, so nothing is waiting on this row for grading.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY ===
I did not promote it, and I did not narrow the DoD to the half that IS reachable (constraint 2 alone). Landing a kind-deriving `lineageFactsFor` while the producer stays single-node would still never reach COMPLETE — one lineage cannot cover six kinds — so a partial promotion buys a commit and no capability, and it would make the row look addressed while its actual blocker stands. If a governor or human rules the fence may come down, this becomes a normal plannable row and I will take it.

DoD 2 AMENDMENT + PATH CORRECTIONS. architect-fdbab575, 2026-08-29, measured at HEAD 62b4d7f6. This comment is the amendment surface; DoD items are not editable by any architect tool, so grade DoD 2 against the text below.

=== FIRST, TWO OF THE THREE NAMED PATHS DO NOT EXIST. Re-measure before believing any line number. ===
  `apps/daemon/src/scheduler/supersession-dispositions.ts` — NO SUCH FILE. The six-kind demand and the duplicate rejection live in **packages/scheduler/src/supersession/supersession-dispositions.ts**, at :65 (`new Set(kinds).size !== kinds.length || new Set(keys).size !== keys.length`) and :78 (`SUPERSESSION_DISPOSITION_KINDS.some((kind) => !present.has(kind))`).
  `apps/daemon/src/planning/lineages.ts` — NO SUCH FILE. The always-PARTIAL answer is **apps/daemon/src/planning/supersession-preparation-lineages.ts**, :64 `if (built.ok) return { coverage: "COMPLETE", digest: built.digest };` / :69 `return { coverage: "PARTIAL", digest: digestOf("lineages", lineages) };`, fed by :63 `buildSupersessionDispositions(lineageFactsFor(lineages))`.
  `journey-authority-bodies.ts` IS correct, but the throw is at :157-161, not :158-161.

=== DoD 4 IS CONSISTENT WITH THE RULING. I checked this first because it looked like a contradiction and it is not. ===
DoD 4 keeps the six-kind requirement and the duplicate rejection UNCHANGED; governor-fd35a081's ruling (comment-6a8d5bd8) retires "the PREPARATION's six-kind coverage fact". Those are different things and both hold: the FENCE stays where it is, in the scheduler builder, and what changes is that the PREPARATION stops using it as a coverage oracle. graph-supersede-dispositions.ts's own header states the split — `buildSupersessionDispositions` "is used by the preparation for its coverage fact", while "the KERNEL asks only for a non-empty set of uniquely keyed, well-shaped entries." Nothing in this row removes a fence, so DoD 4's mutation arms stand as written.

=== DoD 2 DOES CONFLICT WITH THE RULING, AND THE RULING WINS ===
DoD 2 as filed requires: "`lineageFactsFor` derives its kind from durable state rather than a hardcoded literal, and journey-authority-bodies accepts the node ids a real multi-node supersession presents."
The ruling explains why the hardcode is CORRECT, not a defect: "COMPLETE means PER-LINEAGE completeness, measured at SUPERSEDE time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes. That is a correction of WHERE the property is measured, not a relaxation of the standard: **at prepare time the successor does not exist, which is exactly why lineageFactsFor has to hardcode ADD**."
So making `lineageFactsFor` derive a kind at PREPARE time would require inventing a successor that does not yet exist — fabricated authority, and epic rail 4 forbids it. Widening `journey-authority-bodies` to accept multiple node ids to feed that derivation is the same error one layer down: the header at :154-156 records the single-node graph as a deliberate content-identity property, not a limitation ("two journeys naming different nodes seal different graphs rather than colliding on one content-addressed body row").

DoD 2, AS IT NOW READS:
"A PRODUCTION path emits per-lineage disposition facts derived at SUPERSEDE time from predecessor + successor node-authority hashes, with no fixture standing in for a writer. The coverage fact moves OFF the prepare-time six-kind oracle and onto that per-lineage derivation. `lineageFactsFor` KEEPS its ADD literal — at prepare time no successor exists, so ADD is the only honest answer and deriving anything else would fabricate one — and `journey-authority-bodies`' single-node-id throw at :157-161 is UNCHANGED, being a content-identity property rather than a limitation.
